title: Use Units and Land Measurements
readerIntent: Configure measured products and stock without mixing dimensions.
priorKnowledge: Know the product and inventory measurement requirements.
owner: Units owns definitions/conversions; consuming modules own business meaning
summary: Define stable units, compatible dimensions, canonical conversion, precision, and rounding before using them in Product or Inventory.

sections.heading: Unit definition
items: Stable code and localized name.
Dimension such as count, mass, volume, length, or area.
Symbol and canonical unit.
Conversion factor or governed conversion service.
Precision, rounding mode, minimum increment, and active state.
Audit and compatibility metadata.

sections.heading: Example: produce by mass
paragraphs: Define kilogram as the canonical mass unit and gram as a compatible unit. A 750-gram receipt normalizes to 0.75 kilogram while preserving 750 grams as original evidence.
Inventory performs stock arithmetic in the normalized unit and displays the configured user-friendly unit.

sections.heading: Example: land and agriculture
paragraphs: A real-estate or agricultural product can use square metre, hectare, acre, or another configured area unit. Product owns parcel attributes and business meaning; Units owns conversion.
Area cannot convert to mass or volume without a domain-owned formula and additional data. Units rejects the dimension mismatch.

sections.heading: Governance and customization
items: Reuse an existing definition before adding a new code.
Add regional display units through project data without modifying conversion algorithms.
Treat factor or canonical-unit changes as migrations because stored normalized values may be affected.
Keep locale formatting in presentation while arithmetic stays locale-neutral.
Restrict who can create or change foundational units.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Forward and reverse conversion.

Rounding at repeated conversion boundaries.
Incompatible dimension and inactive unit rejection.
Original-value audit and locale display.
Product, Pricing, Inventory, import/export, and regression integration.

sections.heading: What This Capability Solves
paragraphs: Units gives every Nodics business module one consistent way to describe quantities and convert units. It supports pieces, weight, liquid volume, distance, land area, percentages, time, and compound quantities such as kilograms per hectare.

Units is reusable functionality, not necessarily a separate application or server. Most projects run it in the same process as Inventory, Product, or Pricing. A dedicated Units deployment is useful only when several independent runtimes need one centrally governed conversion authority.

Always keep the original value and unit supplied by the source. Store a normalized value separately when a consuming module implements normalization. This preserves legal, survey, supplier, scale, and operator evidence.

sections.heading: Important Land Rule
paragraphs: Some traditional land-unit names have different sizes in different places. Never assume a universal conversion for bigha, kanal, marla, cent, guntha, or another regional unit. Supply the country and, where required, state/province or locality. The system rejects ambiguous conversion rather than guessing.

Units does not decide which area is legally correct. A property or farm may separately record registered area, surveyed area, polygon-calculated area, usable area, built-up area, carpet area, cultivable area, or irrigated area. The owning real-estate/agriculture module classifies those values; Units converts them.

sections.heading: Administrator Workflow
paragraphs: The current foundation keeps generated master-data APIs private. An administrator therefore uses the project's governed initialization/import path or a project-provided permissioned administration intent. Nodics does not yet provide a generic human Units-maintenance screen, and projects should not enable generated CRUD as a shortcut.

sections.heading: Beginner Example: Grams To Kilograms
paragraphs: Assume `MASS`, gram (`G`), kilogram (`KG`), and the exact conversion `G_TO_KG` with numerator `1` and denominator `1000` are active. Convert the canonical string `"1000"` from `G` to `KG`, requesting scale `3` and rounding `UNNECESSARY`. The result is `"1.000"`.
Do not send the JavaScript number `0.1`. Send `"0.1"` so the source value has not already lost decimal precision.

sections.heading: Common Business Uses
paragraphs:
| Business need | Units responsibility | Owning business module responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hold `2.500 KG` of stock | Validate `KG` and perform exact conversions | Inventory owns balances and movements |
| Sell liquid by litre | Define `VOLUME`, `L`, and governed conversions | Product describes it; Pricing owns price; Inventory owns quantity |
| Store package dimensions | Validate length and weight Unit codes | Product owns packaging meaning |
| Price by kilogram or square metre | Supply the Unit basis and conversions | Pricing owns price selection and money |
| Compare acres and hectares | Convert compatible AREA values | Land/agriculture owns area type and evidence |
| Express kilograms per hectare | Validate a compound dimension vector | Agriculture owns yield meaning |

sections.heading: Developer Rules
paragraphs: Pass decimal values as strings, never JavaScript numbers. Declare target scale and rounding. Use `UNNECESSARY` when loss of precision must stop the operation. Compare dimension vectors before conversion. Retain conversion identity, geography, effective time, original value/unit, and normalized result in business evidence when the consuming module implements persistence.
Customize through later modules and the `units` properties. Do not create separate UOM tables or conversion services inside Inventory, Product, Pricing, agriculture, or real-estate modules.

When modules run together, they invoke the Units intent service locally. When Units runs separately, they call its service-token-only conversion route through Nodics module communication. The result and selection rules are the same; operators configure topology through `servers.units`, not by copying Unit data into each domain.
Example remote request:

```http
POST /nodics/units/v0/references/units/convert
Authorization: Bearer <runtime-service-token>
x-enterprise-code: enterpriseA
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "quantity": "1000",
  "fromUnitCode": "G",
  "toUnitCode": "KG",
  "targetScale": 3,
  "roundingMode": "UNNECESSARY"
}
```

The response contains the exact converted quantity plus selected Unit and conversion evidence. Consumers should retain this evidence when the calculation has financial, stock, legal, or audit significance.

sections.heading: What Operators Should Monitor
paragraphs: Track failures by error code, dimension, geography, enterprise, and correlation identifier. Monitor latency and availability when Units is remote. Avoid logging sensitive quantities, prices, or parcel details merely to diagnose a conversion.

Back up Dimensions, Units, and Conversions together. Restore Dimensions first, then Units, then Conversions. Test representative business volume in the actual deployment; framework correctness tests are not universal capacity evidence.
